## 7. Hidden-set selection rule (frozen, verbatim)

```
HIDDEN-SET SELECTION RULE — the hidden 1,000 are derived, never chosen:

1. At freeze time a 256-bit secret seed S is drawn from the OS CSPRNG.
   S is never published, logged, or embedded in any
   participant-visible artifact until the post-scoring reveal.
2. For each of the 5,000 corpus PMCIDs (literal string, e.g. 'PMC6939896'),
   compute D(PMCID) = HMAC-SHA256(key=S, msg=PMCID), lowercase hex.
3. Sort the 5,000 (D, PMCID) pairs ascending by D (lexicographic on the
   hex string); break ties by PMCID ascending.
4. The first 1,000 PMCID values in that order are the hidden evaluation set.
5. hidden-1000.txt lists those 1,000 PMCIDs in derivation order, one
   per line, no header, LF line endings.
6. Commitment C = sha256(S_raw_32_bytes + hidden-1000.txt bytes),
   published as hidden-1000.sha256 at freeze time. C binds the seed AND
   the list. After scoring closes, S (hex) and hidden-1000.txt are
   published; anyone can recompute the derivation from the manifest
   corpus list and verify C.
7. The hidden LIST and the seed S never appear in any public-facing file;
   only the commitment C is published at freeze time. Without S the
   hidden set is not computable from any public artifact.
```
